descriptionChirho: Negative particle functioning as preposition or adverb expressing privation or absence; used alone (בְּלִי 'without'), or in combination with prefixed prepositions: מִבְּלִי 'for lack of, because there is no', בִּבְלִי 'without', לִבְלִי 'so as not to, lest', כִּבְלִי 'as without'; also with interrogative ה in the rhetorical formula הַמִבְּלִי 'is it because there is no...?'; and in the temporal phrase עַד־בְּלִי 'until there is no more, forever'

Substantival use denoting nothingness or annihilation, as in שַׁחַת בְּלִי 'pit of nothingness/destruction' (Isa 38:17), where בְּלִי functions as a noun rather than a preposition, expressing the concept of utter non-existence
